summary.text: A 31-year-old woman went to the hospital on 1 June 2017 with fatigue and dizziness for 1 month that had worsened over the past week. Hemoglobin was 38 g/L at the emergency department and esophagogastroduodenoscopy showed chronic superficial gastritis. Severe anemia persisted after blood replenishment treatment, so she was hospitalized with anemia of unknown origin.

Workup showed hemoglobin 45 g/L, urine red blood cells, positive stool occult blood and erythropoietin above 762.00 mIU/ml. Capsule endoscopy showed polypoid proximal jejunal mucosa with active bleeding, and deep enteroscopy showed granular erosive mucosa; biopsy pathology showed chronic inflammation and cystic dilatation of lymphatic vessels.

She received surgical treatment on 14 June 2017, with removal of a 17 cm intestinal segment, and pathology gave a diagnosis of small intestinal lymphangioma with no lesion at the resection end. She left the hospital after anti-inflammatory and nutritional support treatment, recovered well and had no recurrence so far.

summary.text: A 52-year-old woman went to the hospital on 3 November 2020 with recurrent upper abdominal pain for more than 20 days, paroxysmal and knife-like. Examination showed tenderness in the middle and right upper abdomen without rebound pain or muscle tension, and the admission diagnosis was abdominal pain of unknown origin. Blood routine, CRP, biochemistry, AFP, CA19-9 and CEA showed no abnormalities.

Abdominal CT showed local intestinal wall edema and mesenteric edema. Capsule endoscopy showed ileal lesions with continuous nodular mucosal changes, and contrast-enhanced CT of the small intestine showed segmental terminal ileal wall thickening suggesting possible inflammatory bowel disease. After imaging consultation Crohn disease was suspected, but the clinical course did not conform to its typical manifestations.

She underwent surgical treatment on 1 December 2020, with a 38 cm intestinal segment removed. Pathology indicated small intestinal lymphangioma with no cancer at both ends. She left the hospital after anti-inflammatory and nutritional support therapy, recovered well and had no recurrence so far.
